decisions.decision: Keep Amanda Construction for the South Cemetery stone work, capped at $9,999 (not to exceed) to stay under the competitive-bid threshold.

Rate increases targeted to take effect July 1, aligned with the fiscal year; the roughly 10-12 people already interested in buying lots will be asked to put down money to lock in the current $800 rate before the increase.

Proceed with a reduced first phase of the North Cemetery expansion (roughly half the planned area, starting from the wall/road side) to fit available capital funds, with the contractor asked to add tree plantings and plot-corner markers.
A prior seasonal volunteer will return in mid-June for a few months; the commission will keep trying to fill a second seasonal position.
Pursue getting a more regular, recurring Department of Corrections work crew, possibly one day a week.
Next commission meeting set for Friday, June 5th at 8:00 am, after several proposed dates were ruled out due to a member's travel.
Flag placement for Memorial Day set for Saturday, May 16th, with volunteers including a DPW worker and possibly high school students.
A flag retirement/burning ceremony organized by John Bowen Jr. is being planned for around June 14th, pending his own approach to the town's Board of Selectmen.
Split the cemetery's governing document into 'rules and regulations' aimed at lot purchasers and a separate 'policies' document covering maintenance matters, before updating the town website.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission plans to raise lot, burial and cremation fees starting July 1, after comparing rates charged by nearby towns.
People already interested in buying a lot will be asked to put down money to lock in the current rate before it rises.
The North Cemetery expansion will proceed as a reduced first phase, roughly half the planned area, to fit available capital funds.
The commission kept its South Cemetery stonework contractor, with the job capped at an amount just under the threshold that would trigger competitive bidding.
The commission began splitting its governing document into rules for lot buyers and separate internal maintenance policies.

why_it_matters: Anyone planning to buy a cemetery lot, or arrange a burial or cremation in Lunenburg, will pay a higher fee once the July 1 increase takes effect.
Scaling back the North Cemetery expansion to fit capital funds means less new burial space is built now than originally planned.
Keeping a contract just under the bidding threshold is a procurement choice the commission can make without a competitive bid process.
watch_next: July 1 effective date for the new lot, burial and cremation fees
Next Cemetery Commission meeting, Friday, June 5 at 8:00 am

The two records agree on most decisions in outline — the North Cemetery expansion's reduced first phase (~$140K), the July 1 rate increase with lock-in, the June 14th flag ceremony, and the second seasonal hire still open — but the official minutes are much thinner on figures, and several items are framed differently enough (South Cemetery stone work, the DOC crew's frequency, the Memorial Day flag plan, the governing-document discussion, and the $20k transfer) that a reader should check the recording before treating either account as settled.
